key_insight: Learned models predict high-quality QAOA angles in a single forward pass, replacing costly per-instance optimization with near-identical solution quality.
engineering_relevance: For repeated optimization of similar problems, angle prediction can amortize upfront data-generation and training costs while accelerating QAOA workflows.
method: Learn a mapping from problem instances to QAOA variational angles.
Replace the classical angle optimizer with model inference.
Use topology-sensitive models to improve angle quality.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports inference several orders of magnitude faster than the solver, generalization to unseen Barabási–Albert and 2D grid topologies, and hardware samples indistinguishable from those using solver angles.
watch_item: Upfront data-generation and training costs must be amortized, and generalization beyond the tested problem distributions remains uncertain.
paper_title: Learning angles for quantum approximate optimization
